headline: Christopher Tufton: Tobacco Control Bill should not face endless delay
dek: Writing in the Jamaica Gleaner, Christopher Tufton said the Tobacco Control Bill is needed to close gaps left by the 2013 regulations, citing youth smoking and vaping figures.
body:
Christopher Tufton wrote in a commentary in the Jamaica Gleaner that Jamaica needs to move forward with its Tobacco Control Bill. He was responding to the newspaper's 14 November editorial, "Confronting the quiet respiratory crisis", on chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). He said COPD remains among Jamaica's leading causes of death and welcomed the editorial's identification of tobacco use as its primary driver.

Tufton cited the World Health Organization (WHO) as saying second-hand smoke kills approximately 1.3 million people worldwide each year, and that there is no safe level of exposure. He also said WHO warns that e-cigarette emissions contain nicotine and other toxic substances that can harm users and bystanders.

He pointed to the most recent Global Youth Tobacco Survey, which he said found that 11.7 per cent of Jamaican students aged 13 to 15 use e-cigarettes and 11.2 per cent smoke conventional cigarettes. Nearly one-third reported exposure to tobacco smoke at home and almost half in enclosed public places.

Tufton described the Public Health (Tobacco Control) Regulations of 2013 as an important advance, but said they do not comprehensively address tobacco advertising, promotion and sponsorship, point-of-sale displays, sales to and by minors, or the market for vaping products. Jamaica joined the WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control in 2005.

He said he tabled the bill in 2020 and that it has since been reviewed by a Joint Select Committee of Parliament. He said scrutiny is healthy and that legislators have rightly debated penalties and scope. According to Tufton, the bill would restrict the marketing of tobacco products to young people, prohibit sales to minors and bring e-cigarettes and other emerging nicotine products within the law, including restrictions on their use in public spaces.
key_quote: But careful examination should not become endless delay.

source.title: Christopher Tufton | Protecting Jamaicans from tobacco’s quiet toll
